Cornwall by Motorcycle: Britain's Subtropical Coast

Cornwall is where England gets dramatic. The Atlantic pounds the north coast, creating rugged cliffs and surf beaches. The south coast is gentler, with hidden coves and fishing villages. In between, narrow lanes wind through a landscape that feels more Mediterranean than British. A Cornish motorcycle tour is a feast for the senses.

The North Coast: Atlantic Highway

The A39 Atlantic Highway from Bude to Newquay is Cornwall's signature riding road. It follows the coast at a distance, with frequent turnoffs to cliff-top villages and beaches. The road itself is fast and flowing, with long straights and sweeping bends. Tintagel (legendary birthplace of King Arthur) and Padstow (Rick Stein's seafood empire) are essential stops.

Land's End Circuit

The B3306 from St Ives to Land's End is Cornwall's wildest road. Hugging the cliff edge through mining country, it passes through Zennor, Morvah, and Sennen. The landscape is stark and windswept — old mine engine houses dot the headlands and the sea stretches to the Americas. Land's End itself is touristy but the surrounding coast is magnificent.

The South Coast: Hidden Cornwall

The south coast from Falmouth to Looe is gentler but equally beautiful. The Roseland Peninsula is one of Cornwall's best-kept secrets — quiet lanes through sub-tropical gardens and hidden creeks. The Lizard Peninsula is Britain's most southerly point and features the spectacular coast road to Kynance Cove.

Cornwall's narrow lanes and high hedges can be challenging on a motorcycle. Approach blind bends cautiously — tractors, horses, and campervans appear without warning.

Suggested 4-Day Route

  • Day 1: Cross the Tamar at Launceston, ride the Atlantic Highway to Padstow. Overnight Padstow
  • Day 2: Padstow to St Ives via Newquay and Perranporth. Overnight St Ives
  • Day 3: B3306 to Land's End, then south coast to Falmouth. Overnight Falmouth
  • Day 4: Lizard Peninsula loop, then east through Fowey and Looe back to Devon

Practical Tips

Cornwall is extremely busy in July and August — roads become congested, especially the A30 and approaches to popular beaches. Visit in May-June or September-October for the best experience. The weather is milder than the rest of England — Cornwall rarely gets snow, and spring arrives weeks earlier than up north. Fuel stations are plentiful but some remote areas have limited opening hours. Watch for sand and gravel on coastal roads, especially after storms. keyTakeaways: The A39 Atlantic Highway from Bude to Newquay is Cornwall's signature fast, flowing coastal road.
The B3306 from St Ives to Land's End is Cornwall's wildest road, hugging cliff edges through mining country.
The gentler south coast from Falmouth to Looe includes the Roseland and Lizard peninsulas.
A suggested 4-day route runs the Tamar to Padstow, St Ives, Falmouth and the Lizard loop.
Cornwall is extremely busy in July and August, so visit May to June or September to October.

faq.q: What is Cornwall's best coastal road?
faq.a: The A39 Atlantic Highway from Bude to Newquay is the signature ride, fast and flowing with long straights, sweeping bends and frequent turnoffs to cliff-top villages. For wilder riding, the B3306 from St Ives to Land's End hugs the cliff edge through stark mining country and is Cornwall's most dramatic road.

Avoid July and August if you can, when roads become congested, especially the A30 and approaches to popular beaches. Visit in May to June or September to October for the best experience. The weather is milder than the rest of England, so spring arrives weeks earlier and snow is rare.

faq.q: What hazards should I watch for?
faq.a: Cornwall's narrow lanes and high hedges are challenging, so approach blind bends cautiously as tractors, horses and campervans appear without warning. Watch for sand and gravel on coastal roads, especially after storms, and allow extra time because progress on the minor roads is slower than the map suggests.

faq.q: How long do I need to tour Cornwall?
faq.a: A satisfying loop takes about four days: cross the Tamar to the Atlantic Highway and Padstow, ride to St Ives via Newquay, take the B3306 to Land's End and on to Falmouth, then loop the Lizard Peninsula and head east through Fowey and Looe. Longer allows deeper exploration of hidden coves.
